model_annotation: The provided figure features three pie charts illustrating the distribution of quantifiers and operations across different reasoning types, specifically categorized as Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, and Disjunctive & Conjunctive. None of the charts utilize a separate legend or visually exploded exterior slices; instead, all category labels and corresponding exact percentage values are positioned directly within the segments, with the category text appearing slightly bolder than the numerical values below it. The first chart, titled "Categorical", contains four colored slices: a light blue slice for "Universal Quantifiers" (29.07%), a light pink slice for "Limiter" (27.91%), a light orange slice for "Negation" (27.91%), and a light green slice for "Existential Quantifiers" (15.12%). The second chart, "Approximate Number Generation", consists of three slices arranged clockwise in descending size order: a light yellow segment for "Approximate Quantities" (45.03%), a light blue segment for "Comparative Relationships" (36.26%), and a light purple segment for "Absolute Absence" (18.71%). The third chart, "Disjunctive & Conjunctive", is divided into two roughly equal sections containing a light pink slice for "Conjunctive" (50.49%) and a light grey-purple slice for "Disjunctive" (49.51%).
